summary: The article argues that education and skill development are now a continuous, lifelong process because of rapid economic and technological change. It surveys the roles of technology (including VR), soft skills, governments, corporations, universities and individuals in building an adaptive workforce, citing reports, speakers and initiatives from late 2023 to mid-2024.
one_line: A news feature on how technology, governments, companies, universities and individuals are driving lifelong learning to close the skills gap in a changing economy.
key_facts: The Institute for Future Workforce Development report of November 10, 2023 stated that 85% of the jobs that will exist in 2030 haven't been invented yet.
Emily Johnson, an educational reformer, spoke at the Global Skills Summit on December 15, 2023, saying education must be seen as 'a fundamental aspect of our lifestyle' rather than a phase.
A TechLearning study released January 20, 2024 found virtual reality (VR) has revolutionized skill development by letting learners practice in safe, simulated real-world scenarios.
Sarah Thompson, a VR educational specialist, said VR creates immersive learning for professions from surgeons to electricians.
Leadership coach David Lee led a webinar on March 3, 2024 for emerging managers, stressing leadership, empathy and collaboration as soft skills.
The European Skills Agenda, updated September 5, 2023, aims to support skill enhancement and re-skilling in the EU, with a focus on digital skills.

The U.S. Department of Education announced initiatives on October 14, 2023 to foster partnerships among educational institutions, industry and non-profits; Secretary Michael Anderson spoke of building a resilient workforce.
Google's certification programs, detailed February 2, 2024, cover data analytics, project management and user experience design.
Amazon's Upskilling 2025 program, amplified June 30, 2024, aims to equip over 100,000 employees with skills for more advanced roles, according to Danielle Brown, VP of Learning and Development.
The Academic Leaders Forum on Education Innovation unveiled a blueprint for modernizing higher education on September 12, 2023, including AI and blockchain courses and flexible degrees.
MIT has introduced modular learning and cross-disciplinary programs; Prof. Alice Garten heads its Curriculum Development Committee.
Jonathan Carter moved from software engineer to product manager through online courses and workshops, illustrating personal accountability.
